Educational outcomes for youths with ADHD reveal a substantial gap when compared to the general population. According to data tracking individuals who turned 17 in 2024, the rate of passing the primary school leaving exam (*folkeskolens afgangsprøve*) is notably lower for those who have been evaluated for or treated for ADHD than for their peers in the broader demographic.

Within the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]], which tracks data from its inception on January 1, 2013, the [[adhd-udredningspopulation|ADHD-udredningspopulation]] shows that only 53% of the young people who were evaluated for ADHD and turned 17 in 2024 successfully passed their primary school leaving exam [^src1]. The outcomes are slightly better for those who actually entered treatment; the [[adhd-behandlingspopulation|ADHD-behandlingspopulation]] data indicates that 58% of the youths who started an ADHD treatment course and turned 17 in 2024 passed the exam [^src1].

In stark contrast, the [[baggrundspopulationen-2023|Baggrundspopulationen 2023]] demonstrates a much higher success rate, with 84% of young people in the general background population passing the primary school leaving exam before the age of 17 [^src1]. This highlights a significant educational disparity, underscoring the systemic challenges faced by students with ADHD in completing their foundational education compared to the general public.
